research.title: Regularized Prediction with Correlated and Missing Covariates
bullets: Designed simulation experiments varying feature correlation and missingness mechanisms to compare regularized regression models under matched training and evaluation conditions.
Analyzed prediction errors and coefficient stability across repeated samples, separating sensitivity to imputation choices from sensitivity to regularization strength.

research.title: Probability Calibration under Distribution Shift
bullets: Designed comparative experiments evaluating probability calibration methods under class prevalence shifts, varying calibration sample size and classifier family.
Analyzed proper scoring rules, reliability diagrams, and subgroup calibration patterns to characterize tradeoffs between aggregate calibration and performance across shifted populations.

work.title: Batch Data Validation and Reporting Utilities
bullets: Implemented assigned Python utilities for validating incoming tabular records, handling malformed fields, and generating summaries for existing internal reporting workflows.
Added regression tests for parsing and validation behavior, investigated reported processing failures, and documented expected inputs and error handling.

projects.title: Comparative Evaluation of Linear and Nonlinear Classification Models
bullets: Implemented classification pipelines using logistic regression, support vector machines, and random forests, with preprocessing fitted exclusively on training partitions.
Compared predictive discrimination and probability quality using stratified cross-validation, examining how feature scaling and hyperparameter selection affected each model.

projects.title: Bootstrap and Analytic Confidence Intervals for Regression
bullets: Implemented residual bootstrap, pairs bootstrap, and analytic confidence intervals for linear regression using Python and NumPy.
Compared empirical coverage and interval width across simulated noise distributions, assessing sensitivity to heteroscedasticity and departures from Gaussian errors.
